title: Read a version 0 PSBT and apply every first-signer rule that needs no key
intent: ADR 0004 (accepted 2026-11-15) fixes what the first signer accepts, and names this as its first task: a PSBT version 0 reader in `firmware/wallet-core` with every rule that needs no key (format, version, size and money limits, hash type and address kinds). It returns either a summary (what each output pays, and the fee) or exactly one refusal that names its reason. A hostile computer attacks this boundary first, so the reader refuses rather than guesses, never panics, holds no key and uses no heap. Key paths, ownership and change checks, signing, the seed, the screen and the transport are later tasks.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `psbt::Psbt::parse` reads raw PSBT bytes and refuses, with a named `PsbtError`: wrong magic, truncation, a length not in its shortest form or above 0x02000000, a duplicate key in any map, no unsigned transaction, an unsigned transaction that `tx::Tx::parse` refuses (this includes witness form and zero inputs) or that has a non-empty scriptSig (BIP174:102), a version field other than 0, fewer input or output maps than the transaction has inputs or outputs, a known key type whose key data or value has the wrong shape (BIP174:97-337, BIP371:46-140), a non-witness UTXO whose txid or output index does not match the input's outpoint (BIP174:431; Knots src/psbt.h:1182-1185), and bytes left over.
A key type the reader does not check, proprietary fields and the global xpub included, parses and stays in place: every map exposes its pairs in their original order and bytes (BIP174:544-546).

ADR 0004 row 8: a PSBT over 65,536 bytes is refused before it is read, and one whose transaction has more than 16 inputs or more than 16 outputs is refused before any input or output map is read. Each limit has a test at the bound and one past it.

`policy::check` returns `Ok(Checked)` or exactly one `Refusal` naming the ADR 0004 refusal line it applies: no output; an input without `PSBT_IN_WITNESS_UTXO`, or whose spent output is not P2WPKH; a non-witness UTXO whose output differs from the witness UTXO; a declared hash type other than 0x21; an input already signed or finalized, or carrying a redeem script, witness script, hash preimage or taproot field; an output that is not P2WPKH, P2WSH, P2TR, P2PKH or P2SH; a money limit (each amount and each total at most 2,100,000,000,000,000 satoshis, outputs not above inputs, fee at most 10,000,000 satoshis).
`Checked` reports the total spent, the fee and every output's index, kind, script and amount, and claims nothing about change; key paths and change are rows 2, 5 and 7, which need keys.

Every refusal in ac-1, ac-3 and ac-4 has two tests built from one documented base vector: a case just inside the rule that is accepted (or refused only for another, named reason) and a case just outside it that is refused for exactly this reason. Each case's comment names the single field it changes.

Knots `test/functional/data/rpc_psbt.json` at the pinned release (commit a7c4617524c334f542484bfef3919b9f12573840, git blob 1ccc5e0ba0c1945f243dbedbcc6163b5a202a08d, SHA-256 898f22ccc12e2f1f5b4476eb5e742d6fe180b9a38d60c844470d5d72884b140e) is copied unchanged into `firmware/wallet-core/tests/data/` with a provenance note and a hash test. Every `invalid` and `invalid_with_msg` entry that is valid base64 is refused by `policy::check`; every `valid` entry except the one with zero inputs parses with `Psbt::parse`.

No input makes the reader panic: a test checks every prefix of every vector, and every single-byte change of the base vector, and requires a result without a panic. No `unsafe`, no heap, no new dependency, no change to the workspace lints, and `sighash.rs` and its fixture are unchanged.

`bash scripts/gates/firmware-check.sh`, `npm test` and `git diff --check` pass at the reviewed commit, and `python3 .github/skills/device-references/scripts/unified_sighash_check.py firmware/wallet-core/tests/data/unified_sighash.json` gives the same result as on main.

risk.rationale: This code decides which PSBTs reach the signer. A rule it lets through is a payment a hostile computer can hide, so the owner approves the plan before implementation (approvals.yaml, high risk) and a security audit from another model family than the implementer's is required (ADR 0003).
